title: 2025 AMC 10B Problem 12
statement:
The figure below shows an equilateral triangle, a rhombus with a \(60^\circ\) angle, and a regular hexagon, each of them containing some mutually tangent congruent disks. Let \(T,\) \(R,\) and \(H,\) respectively, denote the ratio in each case of the total area of the disks to the area of the enclosing polygon.

Which of the following is true?

solutions.text: Take the triangle with side \(s.\) Three disks of radius \(r\) give \(s = 2r(1 + \sqrt3),\) so \(T = \dfrac{3\pi r^2}{(\frac{\sqrt3}{4})s^2}\) \(= \dfrac{(2\sqrt3 - 3)\pi}{2} \approx 0.73.\) For the rhombus with side \(a,\) the two disks sit on the long diagonal \(a\sqrt3 = 6r,\) so \(r = \tfrac{a}{2\sqrt3}\) and \(R = \dfrac{2\pi r^2}{(\frac{a^2\sqrt3}{2})} = \dfrac{\pi\sqrt3}{9} \approx 0.60.\) For the hexagon with side \(a,\) each of the six disks touches a side at its midpoint, again giving \(r = \tfrac{a}{2\sqrt3}\) and \(H = \dfrac{6\pi r^2}{(\frac{3\sqrt3}{2})a^2}\) \(= \dfrac{\pi\sqrt3}{9} \approx 0.60.\) So \(H = R \lt T.\) Therefore, the answer is C.
hints: For a disk tangent to two sides meeting at angle \(\theta,\) its center is at distance \(\dfrac{r}{\sin(\frac{\theta}{2})}\) from the vertex
Use the tangency conditions to write each disk radius \(r\) in terms of the polygon’s size, then compute (disk area) / (polygon area) in each case
